deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page is a set of tables of the biquadratic (quartic) residue character in Z[i], plus a four-case rule. On the previous page (the (t+iu)(A+iB)/(a+ib)=x+iy computation and the square split into four parts) Gauss is working on a lattice-point / Gauss-lemma criterion for the quartic character. These tables look like the numerical data for that work and for checking biquadratic reciprocity.

A. TABLES OF THE QUARTIC CHARACTER. Each block has the same layout. First comes a Gaussian prime pi=a+bi of norm p≡1 (mod 4). Next is a rational integer r with r ≡ i (mod pi): solve a+br≡0 (mod p), so r ≡ -a/b. Then the residues 1..p-1 mod p are split into four classes k=0,1,2,3. Class k is the set of n with n^((p-1)/4) ≡ r^k (mod p), i.e. the quartic character (n/pi)_4 = i^k.

After that come small Gaussian primes and units, assigned to classes. Each z=c+di is reduced to c+dr (mod p) and put in its class. The list is 1, i, -1, 1±i, 3, 1±2i, -3±2i, 1±4i, 5±2i, 1±6i, 5±4i, ±7, 5±6i, -7±2i, -3±8i, 5±8i, 9±4i, 1±10i. These are all Gaussian primes of norm ≤101, normalized mostly with b even and a≡1 (mod 4), with the modulus itself omitted.

Block by block (my verification):
- pi=3+2i, p=13, r=5 (3+10=13). (p-1)/4=3. Classes: 0:{1,3,9}, 1:{7,8,11}, 2:{4,10,12}, 3:{2,5,6}. Example: -7+2i -> -7+10=3, class 0.
- pi=1+4i, p=17, r=4. Classes: 0:{1,4,13,16}, 1:{6,7,10,11}, 2:{2,8,9,15}, 3:{3,5,12,14}. Here i and -1 are in class 0, since p≡1 (mod 8).
- pi=5+2i, p=29, r=12 (-5/2 = -5·15 ≡ 12). (p-1)/4=7. Classes: 0:{1,7,16,20,23,24,25}, 1:{2,3,11,14,17,19,21}, 2:{4,5,6,9,13,22,28}, 3:{8,10,12,15,18,26,27}.
- pi=1+2i, p=5, r=2. Classes {1},{2},{4},{3}; the Gaussian primes are distributed accordingly.
- pi=1+6i, p=37, r=6. (p-1)/4=9. Only the rational classes are given (four classes of 9).
- pi=5+4i, p=41, r=9. (p-1)/4=10. Four classes of 10.
- pi=-7+2i, p=53, r=30 (7·27=189≡30, and 30^2≡-1). (p-1)/4=13. Four classes of 13.

B. THE FOUR-CASE RULE. My interpretation: (x) is the integral part, so x=(x)+xi and y=(y)+eta with 0≤xi,eta<1. Then x-y-(x)+(y)=xi-eta and x+y-(x)-(y)=xi+eta, i.e. the components of (1+i)(xi+i·eta). Taking the integer part {} of each gives four possibilities:
- (0,0): xi≥eta, xi+eta<1 (bottom triangle);
- (0,1): xi≥eta, xi+eta≥1 (right triangle);
- (-1,1): xi<eta, xi+eta≥1 (top triangle);
- (-1,0): xi<eta, xi+eta<1 (left triangle).
The two diagonals thus cut the unit square into four triangles, read counterclockwise as classes 0,1,2,3. This matches the 'square divided into four parts' and the class table x:0110, y:0011 on the previous page.

C. PURPOSE. This is the ingredient of a quartic Gauss lemma. Multiply a quarter-system of residues by (t+iu) times a fraction mod (a+ib). Count which quarter (triangle) the fractional part lands in. The total exponent of i gives the quartic character. The tables provide numerical cases to test such a criterion and the biquadratic reciprocity law.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. All rational class lists for p=13,17,29,37,41,53 check: each class has (p-1)/4 elements and together they cover 1..p-1.
Every Gaussian entry checked in the 3+2i, 1+4i, 5+2i and 1+2i blocks is in the correct class.

Several entries that look deleted or blotted are in fact correct: 1+4i in the 3+2i class 1 (≡8), 3 in the 1+4i class 3 (3^4≡13), -1 in the 5+2i class 2, and the blot in the 1+2i class 2 (≡4 if it is -7-2i).

The normalization of the prime list is not uniform. The rational prime appears as 3 or -3 and as 7 or -7 in different blocks, and -i is never listed. Since (-1/pi)_4 = ±1 depending on p mod 8, the table entries are still correct for the numbers actually written.

results.what: Tables of the quartic residue character (n/pi)_4 for Gaussian primes pi of norm 5,13,17,29,37,41,53, for rational residues and for all Gaussian primes of norm ≤101
results.modern_name: biquadratic (quartic) residue symbol tables in Z[i]

results.what: Use of r≡i (mod pi) to reduce Z[i]/(pi) to Z/p, and the quartic character as n^((p-1)/4) compared with powers of r
results.modern_name: Euler criterion for the quartic residue symbol; isomorphism Z[i]/(pi) ≅ F_p

results.what: Four-case rule: the integer parts of the components of (1+i)·(fractional part) locate a point in one of four diagonal triangles of the unit square. This feeds a lattice-point/Gauss-lemma criterion for the quartic character.
results.modern_name: Gauss's lemma for quartic residues (Z[i] analogue of Gauss's lemma)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's Nachlass on biquadratic residues (Werke II); later treated by Eisenstein and others

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss is well known to have computed quartic character tables and to have pursued lattice-point and Gauss-lemma approaches to biquadratic reciprocity in his Nachlass. The four-triangle rule is a nice concrete detail of that work, but not a new result.
